* playwright: allow ensureFeatureFlag to set multiple flags, remove skipIfFeatureFlagNotSet

ensureFeatureFlag now accepts either a single (flagName, value) pair or a
{flagName: value} map, so prerequisites like
'await pw.skipIfFeatureFlagNotSet("ChannelAttributes", true)' can be
combined with other flag prerequisites into a single server restart
instead of one restart per flag.

skipIfFeatureFlagNotSet is removed entirely (definition, export, and
fixture wiring): it only ever skipped a test when a flag was off rather
than turning it on, which silently left specs gated on a flag that
defaults off (e.g. DiscoverableChannels, ManagedChannelCategories)
permanently un-exercised in CI.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: migrate skipIfFeatureFlagNotSet call sites to ensureFeatureFlag

Mechanical rename of skipIfFeatureFlagNotSet(flag, true) to
ensureFeatureFlag(flag, true) across channel_attributes, global_attributes,
board_attributes, channel_perm_rules, and abac specs/helpers. Adjacent
single-flag calls within the same test are merged into one
ensureFeatureFlag({flagA: true, flagB: true}) call so the server restarts
once per test instead of once per flag.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: mark tests broken by real DiscoverableChannels/ManagedChannelCategories as known issues

Both DiscoverableChannels and ManagedChannelCategories default to off and
were never set in the testcontainers CI baseline, so every spec gated on
skipIfFeatureFlagNotSet(flag, true) for these flags silently self-skipped
and never actually ran. Migrating them to ensureFeatureFlag makes the
server restart with the flag genuinely on, which surfaces pre-existing
product bugs:

- discoverable_channels.spec.ts: Browse Channels' search results race the
  typed-search fetch against the discoverable-only loadDiscoverableChannels()
  fetch, intermittently dropping the 'Request to join' button. The sibling
  Find Channels flow is unaffected and still passes.
- managed_categories.spec.ts: assigning a managed_category_name to a
  channel has no effect on the sidebar in this server build - channels
  stay under the regular CHANNELS group and no managed category header is
  ever rendered, so every behavior that depends on being in a managed
  category (grouping, sorting, real-time updates, disabled Favorite/Move
  To/context-menu, and the System Console setting) fails.

Mark the affected tests with test.fixme and a @knownIssue comment so they
report as skipped rather than failing CI, while the two tests that don't
depend on the broken behavior keep running normally.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: force ChannelAttributes off in channel_classification.spec.ts

ChannelAttributes now defaults on (#38937), which hides the legacy
classification toggle this suite exercises (gated on
!channelAttributes.enabled in new_channel_modal.tsx and
channel_settings_configuration_tab.tsx). Force the flag off via
ensureFeatureFlag so the toggle renders again.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: force ChannelAttributes off in channel_banner.spec.ts

Same root cause as channel_classification.spec.ts: with ChannelAttributes
on by default, channel_settings_configuration_tab.tsx renders the
attribute-aware BannerTextEditor instead of the legacy AdvancedTextbox
(testid channel_banner_banner_text_textbox) this suite drives. Force the
flag off via ensureFeatureFlag so the legacy control renders again.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: give permalink preview wait more headroom in initial_scroll_read.spec.ts

The 'with multiple pages of post previews' case waits on a .post-preview
locator with Playwright's implicit 30s default timeout while 120
permalink previews resolve. Under full 30-way parallel CI load this
consistently took 39-44s (observed across two separate dispatch leases
in CI run 37112179268), timing out even though the behavior itself is
correct. Explicitly extend the wait to 60s and the per-test timeout to
90s for this case only.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

Enforces that a Playwright spec file calls ensureFeatureFlag at most
once, and only from a top-level test.beforeAll(). This keeps the
intent of a spec's feature-flag combination explicit at the top of
the file instead of scattered through individual tests, and bounds
each spec file to at most one server restart.

* playwright: mark 3 channel attribute chip-overflow tests as known issues

These three tests fail on master independent of this PR (reproduced
against the committed baseline via git stash, and live against a
Testcontainers server), each from a distinct bug in the
ChannelAttributeLabels/useLabelsOverflow chip-collapse feature:

- 'collapses the thread header chips into +N without moving the
  thread controls': availableWidthForLabels only measures the chip
  row's own flex ancestor, which in the thread pane has no visibility
  into how much room the separate Follow/popout/menu controls need.
- 'collapses overflowing chips into +N without moving header
  controls': channel-header__icons' deliberate min-width:0 lets it
  shrink below what its own non-shrinking icon buttons need, and the
  chip row is forced to show one chip even with zero room left,
  spilling ~12px past the header.
- 'adds and removes a multiselect option, and the header chips
  follow': removing one of two multiselect values leaves the chip
  container permanently visibility:hidden -- useLabelsOverflow's
  debounced recalculation after the ids change never completes.

Each is documented with a @knownIssue explaining the root cause found
via live reproduction, matching the convention already used for the
managed categories known issues.

can combine several prerequisite flags into a single restart instead
of one per flag.

restartMattermostContainer() points the server at a new container and
clears the cached client, so the pre-restart adminClient was stale by
the time it was used to verify the flags took effect. Fetch a fresh
client instead.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: call ensureFeatureFlag per test, remove skipIfNoEnterpriseLicense, fix stale adminClient reuse

Revert the top-level beforeAll/bare-import ensureFeatureFlag calls back
to per-test pw.ensureFeatureFlag() calls, since pw is a test-scoped
fixture and unavailable in beforeAll. Every test in a given spec file
passes the same parameters, so the Testcontainers server still restarts
at most once per file.

pw.skipIfNoLicense().

ensureFeatureFlag's restart was reused afterward: the restart points the
server at a new container, leaving that client stale. Reorder calls so
ensureFeatureFlag runs first, or refresh the client afterward when
reordering is not possible.

* playwright: give permalink preview wait more headroom in initial_scroll_read.spec.ts

the default test timeout under loaded CI. Extend the timeout for that
case to leave headroom on top of the one-minute postPreview.waitFor.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: document ensureFeatureFlag convention and PW_WORKERS in AGENTS.md

Add e2e-tests/playwright/AGENTS.md covering the single-worker-per-server
parallelism model, the ensureFeatureFlag one-restart-per-file convention,
and pw.skipIfNoLicense(). Import it from the root AGENTS.md.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: stop custom profile attribute fields leaking across spec files

attribute_settings_behavior.spec.ts's MM-T5749 test created a custom
profile attribute field named "Cancel Test <id>" and never deleted it,
unlike its sibling spec files. Since CI runs many spec files against
one shared server per job, the field persisted and leaked into every
later test's Profile modal in that job.

Its Edit button's computed accessible name becomes "Cancel Test <id>
Edit" (title + button text via aria-labelledby), which
getByRole('button', {name: 'Cancel'})'s substring match also picked up
alongside the real Cancel button, causing a strict-mode violation in
locked_profile_fields.spec.ts whenever both specs ran in the same job
(reproduced locally by running them back-to-back on one server).

Fixes it two ways:
- Track and delete the fields attribute_settings_behavior.spec.ts owns,
  matching the deleteCustomProfileAttributes cleanup convention already
  used by its sibling spec files.
- Switch profile_modal.ts's cancelButton to getByTestId('cancelButton')
  instead of a substring role-name match, so this class of bug can't
  recur from any other attribute name.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* playwright: give long post-preview show-more check more headroom

The permalink preview needs a second render pass once the linked
post's content arrives before it knows whether to show the collapsed
'Show more' treatment. The default 10s expect timeout left no margin
for that extra round trip under loaded CI, causing this case alone
(out of 26 in the same file) to fail intermittently. Extend to 20s,
mirroring the same permalink-preview timing fix already applied to
initial_scroll_read.spec.ts.

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

commit v11.7.13.message:
E2E/Playwright: fix upgrade-to swap resolving the wrong image in workers (release-11.7) (#39185)

* E2E/Playwright: fix upgrade-to swap resolving the wrong image in workers

TestConfig recomputed serverImage via reloadTestConfig() during the
upgrade swap, but isUpgradeToPhaseProjectSelected() only checked argv,
which workers never inherit. The swap worker fell back to the
persisted from-image instead of SERVER_IMAGE, so the swap left the
from-image running and failed assertRunningContainerImage(). The same
argv-only gap also made mattermostWaitStrategy() skip the migration
log wait for the swap's restart.

Add isUpgradeFromProjectActive()/isUpgradeToPhaseProjectActive(),
worker-safe (env-var-aware) versions used by test_config.ts,
mattermost_container.ts, and stack.ts. Keep the argv-only originals
for playwright.config.ts's one-time preflight checks, which must not
re-trigger inside a dependency project's worker (e.g. upgrade-from's
setup dependency).

Co-authored-by: saturnino <saturnino@mattermost.com>

* E2E/Playwright: mark SVG Markdown image post-height test as fixme

The 'post with an SVG Markdown image' case in post_height.spec.ts flakes
on chrome on this release branch: the SVG's intrinsic size resolves in
two layout-shift steps instead of one, which this test doesn't tolerate.
This is a pre-existing CI flake unrelated to the upgrade-image fix in
this PR.

See: https://test-io.test.mattermost.com/reports/mattermost/pr-39185/911a7c8/playwright-full-enterprise?gh_run_id=38692238983

Co-authored-by: sabril <saturninoabril@users.noreply.github.com>

* E2E/Playwright: make isUpgradePathProjectSelected() worker-safe

This branch's upgrade_env.ts predates master's worker-safe
isUpgradePathProjectSelected() (it still only checked argv), so
resetConfigAndRoles' 'skip resetRoles() during an upgrade-path project'
guard in test_fixture.ts silently failed open in worker processes
(workers don't inherit --project). That let resetRoles() run against
the upgrade-from (release-11.6) server with permissions from this
branch's (release-11.7) default_roles_permissions.ts, which includes
ABAC permissions release-11.6 doesn't recognize, failing every
[setup]/upgrade-from test with 'The role was not valid.'

Mirror master: UPGRADE_PATH_PROJECT_ENV env var, isUpgradePathProjectSelected()
also checks it, and the export function (renamed
exportUpgradePathProjectSelection() to match) sets it alongside the
existing from/to-phase env vars.

pull 38479.body:
#### Summary
`plainExtractor.Extract` read the entire input into memory via `io.ReadAll`, ignoring the `maxFileSize` argument that every other extractor in this package respects (`documentExtractor`, `pdfExtractor`, `archiveExtractor`). Since `plainExtractor` matches any filename not claimed by a more specific extractor, this meant extracting content from a large plain-text-like file (`.csv`, `.txt`, `.log`, etc.) could allocate several times the file's size in a single pass, with no bound.

This PR bounds the read to the smaller of the caller-supplied `maxFileSize` and the extractor's own cap (1MB, matching the truncation the caller already applies to extracted content), using the same `utils.LimitedReaderWithError` pattern used by the other extractors. Since the caller already discards everything past 1MB, behavior for existing files and search results is unchanged.

QA steps:
1. Upload a plain-text-like file (e.g. `.csv`) larger than a few MB with content search/extraction enabled.
2. Confirm the file uploads successfully and its searchable content still reflects the beginning of the file, same as before.

#### Summary

On a licensed server with `SqlSettings.DataSourceReplicas` configured, editing a post immediately after creating it intermittently fails with HTTP 403 **"You do not have the appropriate permissions."** Retrying about a second later succeeds.

The post handlers look the post up through an unpinned read. `DBXFromContext` returns `GetReplica()` unless the request context carries the master flag, so the lookup is served by a replica that has not yet received the row the server wrote to master milliseconds earlier. The edit handlers then report the resulting `store.ErrNotFound` as a permission error.

`PATCH /api/v4/posts/{post_id}` performs three independent `GetSinglePost` calls (`patchPost`, `postPatchChecks`, `app.PatchPost`), and `PUT /api/v4/posts/{post_id}` performs two (`updatePost`, plus `Post().Get()` inside `app.UpdatePost`). Each can lose the race, so this pins at handler entry rather than per call site:

```go
c.AppContext = c.AppContext.With(app.RequestContextWithMaster)
```

pull 38832.body:
#### Summary

`Timestamp` caches `now` in state and only refreshed it from a `setTimeout` when the matched range carried an explicit `updateIntervalInSeconds`. The `Today` / `Yesterday` ranges carry no interval, so nothing ever rescheduled them: a channel left open across local midnight kept rendering `Today` above yesterday's posts, and posting after midnight added a *second* `Today` separator instead of relabelling the older one. Reloading or switching channels remounted the component and hid the problem.

`Timestamp` now schedules a re-render at the next local day boundary whenever the label it produced came from a calendar-period comparison against the current time. The delay is computed with `getMillisUntilNextDay` (new in `utils/datetime.ts`), which uses moment's calendar arithmetic in the user's timezone, so it is correct on the 23- and 25-hour days around DST and on days whose midnight is skipped entirely.

Three things beyond the reported symptom:

- **`week`, `month`, `quarter` and `year` ranges had the same bug.** They are compared as whole calendar periods and also carry no refresh interval, so a `last week` label went stale exactly the way `Today` did. Threads, post previews and pending join requests all render timestamps with those units, so the refresh covers day-or-coarser units rather than just `day`.
- **The new-messages toast needed a fix to stay grammatical.** It composed `{count} new messages {isToday, select, true {} other {since}} {date}` with `isToday`

```release-note
Fixed an issue where relative date separators between posts did not update when the local day changed while a channel stayed open, leaving a stale "Today" separator and creating a second "Today" separator for posts made after midnight.
```

#### Summary
Fixes the Threads view's Unreads tab showing an empty list while the empty state says "You have N thread(s) with unread messages".

**Root cause (client):** `shouldAddThreadId` only adds an incoming thread to a team's list if it's newer than a thread already in that list. For an empty Unreads list, `ids.some(...)` is always false, so the first thread to become unread over the websocket was never added, even though the unread count went up. Always adding to an empty list isn't safe, because "load older" pagination uses the oldest loaded thread as its cursor. This applies to both `RECEIVED_THREAD` and `READ_CHANGED_THREAD`.

- `GET /users/{user_id}/teams/{team_id}/threads` and `GET /users/{user_id}/teams/{team_id}/threads/{thread_id}` now send `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- `GlobalThreads` also refetches unread threads when the unread count changes while the list is empty.

**Also fixed:** The "N thread(s)" link in the empty state pointed to `/threads/undefined` when the list was e


pull 39151.body:
#### Summary
The OpenSearch bulk indexing job could hang forever when a response stream stalled mid-body (observed over HTTP/2 with gzipped responses). The library's bulk indexer flushes with `context.Background()`, so a stalled request blocked its worker indefinitely. Once every worker was stuck, the job never completed and could not be canceled from the UI.

This uses options already built into the standard library and `opensearch-go`, so no new dependency or custom transport is needed:
- All OpenSearch clients now send HTTP/2 health-check pings (`http.HTTP2Config.SendPingTimeout`), so dead HTTP/2 connections are torn down.
- The indexing job's client sets `opensearch.Config.RequestTimeout` to `RequestTimeoutSeconds`. The deadline applies to each attempt and lasts until the response body is closed, so stalled bodies fail over both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. The worker reports the failure and moves on. Other clients are unchanged, so long-running admin calls keep their own timeouts.

A separate commit fixes a nil pointer panic in the shared search logger. With sniffing enabled (the default), a failed initial node discovery logs with a nil request and response, which crashed the server. The logger now also includes the error itself, which was never logged before.

Elasticsearch is intentionally not addressed here: `go-elasticsearch`/`elastic-transport-go` offer no equivalent per-request timeout.

Tests:
- `TestOpenSearchIndexerClientTimesOutStalledResponse` runs the real bulk index

```release-note
Fixed an issue where the OpenSearch bulk indexing job could hang indefinitely when a connection to OpenSearch stalled.
```
